newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean president urges teachers to end strike.
newsitem.headline: Chilean president urges teachers to end strike.

text.p: Chilean President Eduardo Frei called on Tuesday for teachers to end a nationwide strike which has closed schools for over a week after a breakdown in pay talks with the government.
"The only thing we ask is that we sit down and talk," said Frei in a speech during a visit to a school in Santiago.
"With shouts and strikes we won't get anywhere and are condemned to poverty, marginalization and under-development."
While he was speaking, hundreds of striking teachers, waving banners and chanting, marched in streets in downtown Santiago in support of their pay demands.
Over 120,000 teachers are taking part in the protest which has meant more than 2 million schoolchildren have not been attending classes since the strike started a week ago.
The government insisted that its latest offer, which would increase a teacher's minimum monthly wagecheck to 211,300 pesos ($511) for a 30 hour week by 1998, is final.

"The only possibility of an agreement is if they accept this offer which is above wage increases which other professionals in the rest of the public sector receive," said Education Secretary Jaime Perez de Arce.
Union leaders have demanded a minimum monthly wage of 295,000 pesos ($714) within three years. The current minimum is a scant 156,000 pesos ($378).
The strike is the latest in a series of labour disputes which have faced Frei's government this year, including walk-outs in the all-important mining industry.
